name: SmallSQL
tagline: Pure-Java embedded SQL database with a JDBC 3.0 interface for desktop apps; last release in 2011.
description: SmallSQL is a 100% Java relational engine meant to be shipped inside desktop applications: there is no server or network listener, the application opens the database in-process through SmallSQL's JDBC 3.0 driver, and it implements a good share of SQL-92 and SQL-99. Volker Berlin started it in 2005 and published it under the LGPL on SourceForge, where the final 0.21 release appeared in June 2011. It still works as a curiosity or in legacy apps, but H2, HSQLDB and Apache Derby fill the same niche with far broader SQL support and ongoing maintenance.
statusNote: Still downloadable, but the last release was 0.21 (June 2011) and nothing has changed since. H2, HSQLDB or Apache Derby are maintained alternatives.
strengths: Single JAR with no server process or open port
Standard JDBC, so ordinary Java SQL code works against it
LGPL allows bundling inside closed-source desktop applications
weaknesses: No releases since 2011 and no fixes for modern JVMs
No network mode: one application owns a database at a time
Narrower SQL coverage and optimizer than H2 or HSQLDB
useCases: Maintaining legacy Java desktop apps that bundle it
Studying a compact SQL engine implementation
notIdealFor: New Java projects (pick H2 or SQLite)
